content: Entonox, commonly known as gas and air, is an analgesic agent used to alleviate pain during labor, trauma, and minor surgical procedures. It is a proprietary mixture consisting of 50% nitrous oxide (N₂O, also referred to as laughing gas) and 50% oxygen (O₂). Entonox is administered via inhalation, either from a pressurized cylinder (at 137 bar in the UK) or through a pipeline supply. It acts rapidly and its effects dissipate quickly. Nitrous oxide is pharmacologically active in its original form, meaning it does not require metabolic conversion within the body to exert its effects. Its onset of action corresponds to the lung-to-brain circulation time, which is why it is recommended to begin inhalation approximately 30 seconds before a labor contraction becomes painful. The gas is exhaled unchanged through the lungs and does not accumulate in the body under normal conditions, which explains its rapid offset of action. The administration of Entonox does not require the presence of an anesthetist, as the mixture of nitrous oxide and oxygen is pre-determined and controlled. In high doses, nitrous oxide can act as an anesthetic. However, self-administration of Entonox is inherently safe because if a patient inhales enough to induce anesthesia, they will lose the ability to hold the valve, causing them to drop it and exhale the remaining gas. The 50% oxygen content ensures that the patient maintains adequate oxygenation even during a brief period of apnea. At temperatures below 4°C, nitrous oxide and oxygen can separate, potentially leading to the delivery of a hypoxic gas mixture. Therefore, Entonox should never be administered from a cold cylinder. Before use, the cylinder should be inverted several times to ensure proper mixing of the gases. Nitrous oxide is more soluble than oxygen and nitrogen, which allows it to diffuse into air-filled spaces within the body. This property makes it contraindicated in patients with pneumothorax, recent scuba diving activity, or bowel obstruction, as it can exacerbate these conditions. Entonox is manufactured by the BOC Group, which holds the trademark for the product. The ability to combine nitrous oxide and oxygen at high pressure while maintaining their gaseous state is attributed to the Poynting effect, named after the English physicist John Henry Poynting. This phenomenon involves the dissolution of gaseous oxygen when bubbled through liquid nitrous oxide, with subsequent vaporization of the liquid to form a gaseous oxygen/nitrous oxide mixture.
